findings.trigger_condition: The edge stream contains values that compare equal under == but resolve on different identity paths in _id_of: one hashable and one unhashable (e.g. frozenset({1}) vs {1}), or two hashable values equal under == whose hashes differ (a class violating the hash invariant).
findings.root_cause: _id_of partitions node identity by hashability. Hashable values are matched only against other values sharing their hash bucket (hash_buckets.setdefault at line 42, bucket scan at lines 53-56) and never consult the unhashable registry; unhashable values are matched only by the linear scan at lines 44-46 and never enter hash_buckets. Equal values landing on different paths therefore receive distinct node ids even though the module's own dedup model is equality-based (it uses `stored is value or stored == value` within each path).
findings.impact: Verified empirically: dependency_layers([('b', {1}), (frozenset({1}), 'a'), ('a', 'b')]) returns [[{1}], ['b'], ['a'], [frozenset({1})]] instead of raising DependencyCycleError, although {1} == frozenset({1}) makes b -> U -> a -> b a real directed cycle under the equality semantics the implementation otherwise uses. The contract requires raising for a real directed cycle, so genuine cycles can be silently missed. Related milder effects: repeated edges straddling the two paths are not deduplicated, phantom duplicate nodes appear in layers, and dependency ordering constraints are weakened relative to the unified-node interpretation.
findings.suggested_validation: Assert that dependency_layers([('b', {1}), (frozenset({1}), 'a'), ('a', 'b')]) raises DependencyCycleError (or define and test an explicit node-identity rule covering cross-hashability); additionally test dedup of ({1}, 'd') vs (frozenset({1}), 'd') and two ==-equal hashable instances with different hashes.

findings.trigger_condition: An input stream containing many distinct unhashable nodes (lists/dicts/sets), e.g. tens of thousands of unique list nodes.
findings.root_cause: The unhashable fallback resolves every occurrence by a linear scan over all previously registered unhashable nodes (zip over unhashable_ids/unhashable_nodes), giving O(U^2) total comparisons for U distinct unhashable nodes; there is no hashed or sorted index for them.
findings.impact: Quadratic CPU time on unhashable-heavy streams. The stated performance requirement (very deep acyclic inputs without recursion) is still met for hashable nodes — a 50k-node chain was verified to work iteratively — so impact is limited to pathological unhashable workloads.
findings.suggested_validation: Time dependency_layers on ~20k unique list nodes versus ~20k int nodes and compare scaling curves; expect roughly quadratic growth for the unhashable case.
